program.name: The Instrument: TPDB Export
program.summary: The Concrete Witness System, seven constructors and eight rules under the Lean name KO7, is the calculus that carries both axes inside one auditable signature. Its TPDB text rendered from the rule patterns equals the embedded artifact copy, parses back to the declared rules, and is the object TTT2 and CeTA certify.

oneLine: If the verifier main returns 0, both TPDB exporters match their embedded literals and on-disk artifacts.
summary: The theory assembles the public release as a single kernel-checked library and renders TPDB texts for the eight-rule full KO7 root TRS and the two-rule free recursor. It defines minimal TPDB term and rule syntax with renderers for rules, blocks and full VAR and RULES texts, alongside pattern syntax over trace constructors with instantiation and left and right patterns for each kernel rule. The central question is whether the rendered texts reproduce the embedded literals, the embedded artifact copies and the exporter outputs, and whether the artifact copies parse back to the declared variables and syntax trees. The direct renderer outputs coincide with their embedded literals by definition, and the rule lists contain eight and two entries by construction. The pattern-rendered texts equal both the embedded artifact copies and the exporter texts with matching rule lists, while rule instances and root steps coincide with pattern instances for some valuation and rule name. Both artifact copies parse back to the declared variables and rendered rules, with external file parity left to comparison outside Lean and discharged by an IO verifier that returns nonzero on mismatch.
boundary: This theory asserts no separating boundary between provable and unprovable export properties. It certifies reproduction of TPDB texts across renderers, embedded literals and artifact copies. The divide it manages is between inside-Lean rendering and on-disk comparison, with the latter left to comparison outside Lean and discharged by the verifier executable.

For every rule name r and traces t and u, RuleInstance r t u holds if and only if there exists a valuation ρ from naturals to traces with t equal to (ruleLhs r).inst ρ and u equal to (ruleRhs r).inst ρ.

The library root, test checks and build configuration prove no new theorems and aggregate modules, print texts and resolve exact-match theorems, or configure the package, verifier executable and mathlib revision.

files.summary: This file is the Lake library root for the public companion release. It imports the six public API roots covering kernel, schemas, orientation and residual methods. It then imports every remaining published Meta, QEC, RH and Test module so that a single `lake build` kernel-checks the whole release.
files.conclusion: This file proves no theorem and only aggregates all published modules under one build root.

files.summary: The file defines independent pair reductions, a modal Box for persistence, separated and kernel predicates, the off-diagonal observer boundary, reachability and coalescence. It proves that persistent separation is separation of all independent reducts and that its complement is reachability of the kernel, split into diagonal coalescence and boundary collisions. Two counterexamples show a diagonal outside Box without separation or boundary reachability, and a coalescing separated pair without boundary reachability.
files.conclusion: Persistent separation holds for all independent reducts together, and its failure is joint reachability of equal observations split into coalescence or boundary reachability.

files.summary: The file defines finite differentiable experiments passed through a stochastic channel, input and record scores and Fisher informations, variances, residuals and conditional variances, and split scores. It proves Fisher loss equals state minus record information, monotonicity, a record Cramer-Rao product bound under a derivative-one hypothesis, and strictness of the reciprocal floor at shared outputs with different scores, with a deterministic fiber specialization.
files.conclusion: Record information never exceeds state information with gap equal to expected conditional variance, gives the Cramer-Rao product bound, and is strict in the reciprocal bound if and only if split scores occur.

files.summary: The file builds finite Hermitian linear algebra in coordinates, conjugated diagonals, spectral projections and weights, and the scalar resolvent with its Stieltjes sum form. It proves holomorphicity on the upper half-plane, nonnegative imaginary part, and reciprocal-height lower bounds at spectral atoms. It concludes that a nonzero vector and positive scalar preclude any vertically bounded representation on unit segments.
files.conclusion: A finite Hermitian resolvent is holomorphic with nonnegative imaginary part and reciprocal-height atom bounds, so no positive multiple admits a vertically bounded representation for nonzero vectors.

files.summary: The file defines the square grid, Jordan totient counts, normalized gcd kernel, finitely supported coefficient vectors in complex square-summable sequences, and the based kernel and vectors with quadratic forms. It proves the divisor sum identity, the Gram identity for kernel and based kernel, expression of quadratics as sums of squared absolute values, and positivity of both kernels with vanishing at one for the based version.
files.conclusion: The normalized squared-gcd kernel has a finitely supported Jordan-totient Gram realization with nonnegative quadratic forms, and subtracting the feature at one gives the based kernel vanishing at one.

files.summary: The file defines finite rows, binary entropy, cell and gap informations, discrimination, biases with kappa bounds, BSC rows, Bayes and decoder errors, Bhattacharyya coefficients, finite tree experiments and protocols with acquired information and total cost, product rows and bias means. It proves acquired-cost bounds, adaptive squared-bias bounds, product error and eta-threshold information bounds for eta <= 1/2 with an eta = 1 counterexample, and a variance identity with constant-equality characterization.
files.conclusion: Acquired information is bounded by expected discrimination and adaptive squared-bias sums, independent readings have product-BC error and information thresholds, and squared-bias means are tight with equality for constant biases.

files.summary: The file defines 3 by 3 integer tables, six row and column demands, and when a table satisfies a demand. It proves no integer table satisfies all six demands because row products force 1 while column targets force -1. It gives explicit plus-or-minus-one witness tables that satisfy all but any one omitted demand, showing every five-demand subset is realizable and the full set is a minimal obstruction. It also defines finite common laws and proves no finite family of tables admits a distribution giving each demand probability one.
files.conclusion: The six demands form a minimal obstruction with no finite common law giving them all probability one.

files.summary: The file defines a two-place copy model with left and right places, a place-to-role equivalence, and a copy isomorphism identifying pairs with content-role occurrences. It proves the isomorphism is bijective, unique for preserving content and place kernels, and transports separating side-records. It exhibits literal copied subtrees in equality and recursion traces with injective paths, and identifies the positional dependency-pair flag with a callee-subtree test. It proves the flag cannot be factored through content alone and the content-disequality guard is false on both copy pairs.
files.conclusion: The role bijection uniquely identifies matching and duplication occurrences, preserves separation and literal subtrees, and the positional flag separates independently of content.

files.summary: The file defines quadratic forms, positive kernels, Schur complements, the Pick kernel on the upper half-plane, finite Stieltjes transforms, feature vectors and Stieltjes approximability. It proves Gram positivity, preservation of positivity under pointwise limits, Schur positivity with zero base rows, Pick diagonal and sign facts, and the finite Stieltjes Gram and rational-sum formulas. The main theorems give holomorphicity and Pick positivity for finite Stieltjes transforms and the sign, diagonal and Schur conclusions for their pointwise limits.
files.conclusion: Every Stieltjes-approximable function has nonnegative imaginary part, positive Pick kernel, explicit diagonal and Schur complements with zero base rows.

files.summary: The file defines priors, transcript rows, kernels, pointwise and summed error masses, and conditional pair error for definite decision rules. It proves that distinct answers with identical conditional rows force pair error at least the smaller prior, with positivity and conditional bounds, and that pair mass and total error are bounded by one. It proves a constant report of the more probable answer attains the bound and the bound is least.
files.conclusion: Identical transcript laws for distinct answers force pair error at least the smaller prior, attained by constantly reporting the more probable answer.

files.summary: The file defines subrelations, invariance, the box of states with reachable states in the permitted set, safe and controllable edges, and stable and maximal repairs. It proves the box is the greatest invariant subpredicate and maximal repairs are exactly pairs in normal form with all safe edges over the box domain. It proves every uncontrollable subrelation yields such a maximal partition with edge and path comparisons, including fully and never uncontrollable cases.
files.conclusion: Maximal stable repairs are exactly safe restrictions to box domains of uncontrollable subrelations.

files.summary: This file defines a pure-power test and an exact polynomial checker for certificates of the free recursor. It proves that a natural-coefficient interpretation is strictly monotone in every argument exactly when each argument has a positive pure-power monomial, and that the exact checker accepts exactly the unit-slope interpretations that orient both root rules and satisfy all strict context laws. It also proves a boundary theorem that rejects affine, matrix and Knuth-Bendix certificates, agrees with the old checker on multilinear certificates, and accepts the square-wrapper certificate.
files.conclusion: The exact checker accepts precisely the unit-slope polynomial interpretations that orient both root rules and are strictly monotone in every argument, rejecting all affine-keeping, matrix and Knuth-Bendix certificates while accepting the square-wrapper certificate that the old checker rejected.

files.summary: This file proves normalization for the two-rule free recursor on terms with variables in an arbitrary type. It defines bottom-up contextual and root normal-form functions and shows reachability of those forms and their normality. It concludes that both root and contextual rewriting terminate and are confluent, and that joinability in each relation is equivalent to agreement of the corresponding normal forms.
files.conclusion: Root and contextual rewriting of the free recursor terminate and are confluent on terms with variables, with computable normal forms deciding joinability.

files.summary: This file defines direct orienters and a thirteen-family direct universe over every step-duplicating schema. It proves that a uniform orienter of the duplicating step is representable in none of those families. It packages this as an escape trichotomy and as a natural-valued escape theorem for step-duplicating systems.
files.conclusion: No uniform orienter of the duplicating step is representable in any of the thirteen direct families on any step-duplicating schema.

files.summary: This file strengthens the mixed-matrix barrier to strict scalar dominance. It shows that orientation at the base instance supplies the positive scalarized value needed by the nonstrict barrier, so no positivity premise is required. It combines both strict and nonstrict forms and lifts the strict form to global orientation of step-duplicating systems.
files.conclusion: Strict scalar dominance alone rules out uniform orientation of the duplicating step by any mixed-matrix interpretation.

files.summary: The file builds the Gödel side of the LCEL comparison from the compiled Robinson-Q checker. It defines a six-stage ascent profile with the Gödel fixed point at stage two and proves it realizes the six-step shape and is compatible with the dependency-pair profile. It builds formal base, obstruction, framework and reimport semantics from provability and truth in the standard model, with the Gödel sentence as blocked sentence. From these it assembles a comparison object and an LCEL instance, proves the instance realizes the LCEL schema with independent true boundary sentence, and proves six-clause comparisons in both directions with the dependency-pair emitter instance.
files.conclusion: The compiled Gödel LCEL instance realizes the LCEL schema with an independent true boundary sentence and admits six-clause comparisons in both directions with the dependency-pair instance.

files.summary: The file studies the recursor and circular-reference orbit families. It proves the stipulated relation InformationEquivalentModDP holds for every pair of orbits. It defines successor depth and the dependency-pair counter projection and computes its values on the two families. It shows counter-projection agreement is an equivalence relation that separates the two families, while every linear-growth-invariant direct-mass functional agrees on them.
files.conclusion: Every direct-mass functional agrees on the two orbit families while the counter projection separates them.

files.summary: The file studies direct certificates of the duplicating rule in the reflected direct grammar. It defines a direct certificate as a derivable payload-reading expression decreasing across every successor root step. It proves no such certificate exists, so no direct whole-term certificate exists by restriction. It also shows the payload-free counter expression does decrease and the zero rule admits no decreasing profile measure.
files.conclusion: No payload-reading direct grammar expression decreases across the successor rule, so no direct whole-term certificate exists.

files.summary: The file proves two strengthenings free of the concrete kernel. It defines additive whole-term measures with natural weights and proves none orients the duplicating step, already defeated at the step argument of the base. It then proves six coincidence conditions for the four observables on the constant wrapper vector and combines them into a pairwise distinctness characterization with a numeric sample.
files.conclusion: No natural-weighted additive measure orients the duplicating step, and the four observables are pairwise distinct under the stated thresholds with sample values 1, 2, 3, 6.

files.summary: The file adds sound transport maps to certificate hierarchies. It defines transporting hierarchies with acceptance-preserving maps and iterated lift with preservation and soundness above. It defines truth and boundary transports for the free recursor that eliminate low layers by known emptiness. It proves every truth layer at or above one and every boundary layer at or above two holds an accepted termination certificate by transport.
files.conclusion: Accepted termination certificates transport upward so all truth layers from one and all boundary layers from two are inhabited.

files.summary: The file adds the infinite reduction to the Klop system analysis. It defines the term C^n(A) and proves each rewrites to the next by contracting the innermost A. It proves an infinite reduction from A exists and packages no overlap, failure of confluence and the infinite reduction as the contrast for the remark.
files.conclusion: Klop's system is non-overlapping yet non-confluent with an explicit infinite reduction from A.

files.summary: The file proves Lawvere's fixed-point theorem for weakly point-surjective evaluations and deduces no code type carries a diagonal instance with a fixed-point-free endomap. It identifies the confession code object with the one-node type and shows any point-surjective evaluation there has subsingleton values with identity endomaps. It adds controls showing a diagonal datum exists without surjectivity and the kernel successor is fixed-point-free, so the obstruction rests on evaluation.
files.conclusion: No code type, in particular the confession one-node code object, carries a point-surjective evaluation with a fixed-point-free endomap.

files.summary: The file proves the trace law for the free recursor under context closure. For normal base and payload and counter depth k it shows stage terms and the terminal record form the unique maximal derivation with k+1 steps and residual counts. It defines counter, frame and payload readings along the spine and proves their values, offset and sum laws. It shows counter and frames are invariant under payload relabelling while payload count is not, with counter decreasing and frames increasing along the trace.
files.conclusion: From the initial recursor term the unique maximal context-closed derivation follows the stages to the record in k+1 steps with counter-driven residual lengths.

files.summary: The file proves payload invariance of the projected dependency pair for the free recursor. It identifies the successor rule sides and shows extraction keeps the recursive call and no wrapper target is a chain step. It shows the call projection reads the counter argument on both sides and is fixed by every payload relabelling, while a payload relabelling moves the payload argument.
files.conclusion: Dependency-pair extraction drops the wrapper and the counter projection is fixed by all payload relabellings while the payload argument moves.

files.summary: The file calibrates the bounded sentence of the projected pair in first-order arithmetic. It defines successor-closure and induction theories and derives the sentence with successor closure using bound S(c). It builds a two-element successor-escape countermodel with sole number zero that models the eight base axioms and all induction sentences while falsifying the pair sentence. It deduces underivability in all subtheories of induction arithmetic, separation of descent from the pair sentence, and the full calibration with bounded strong normalization.
files.conclusion: Successor closure derives the bounded pair sentence while induction arithmetic does not, calibrating it with bounded strong normalization of the projected pair.

files.summary: The file computes proof-entropy numerator and denominator on leaf-schema live states. It defines payload weight in completed wrappers and proves closed forms for the numerator and weighted size. It identifies both with the abstract entropy functions and proves the cross-multiplied ratio is nondecreasing across live stages with zero payload at stage zero.
files.conclusion: The proof-entropy ratio on live trace states is nondecreasing and starts at zero.

files.summary: The file classifies record emitters into three regimes. It defines the sum type of emitters, the regime map and membership, and proves each emitter lies in a unique regime with each regime inhabited. It defines regime conclusions and proves each emitter satisfies its regime theorem via the classifier.
files.conclusion: Every record emitter lies in a unique regime, each regime is inhabited, and each emitter satisfies its regime conclusion.

files.summary: The file proves three strengthenings on concrete systems. It shows r-ary frames carry r times m plus one payload occurrences. It defines a projection-transaction license from dependency-pair soundness for the free recursor and discharges it with termination. It defines group-action laws for licensed quotients and shows the family-correspondence quotient satisfies them by definition.
files.conclusion: The r-ary payload count holds, the free-recursor projection license is discharged, and the licensed quotient is a group action.

files.summary: This file defines minimal TPDB term and rule syntax with renderers for the full KO7 root TRS and the free two-rule recursor. It declares the eight full-step rules and two recursor rules and builds concrete TPDB strings with VAR and RULES blocks. It proves each renderer output equals its embedded reference literal and that the lists have lengths eight and two. External file parity is explicitly left to comparison outside Lean.
files.conclusion: The Lean-rendered TPDB texts equal the embedded reference literals and have eight and two rules respectively.

files.summary: This file defines rule patterns over trace constructors with instantiation and proves that rule instances and root Step are exactly pattern instances. It renders both TPDB texts from Lean rule objects with computed VAR lines and proves them equal to the embedded artifact copies and exporter texts. It defines a tokenizer and parser for the restricted TPDB syntax and proves both artifact copies parse back to the declared variables and rendered syntax trees.
files.conclusion: The TPDB texts rendered from Lean rule objects equal the exporter texts and parse back to the same syntax trees.

files.summary: This file checks the KO7 TPDB exporter. It prints the full-step and free-recursor TPDB texts and checks their exact-match theorems. It also issues paired #check and #print axioms queries for TPDB terms and rules, rendering functions, rule lists, embedded references and artifact texts, and rule counts. It proves no new theorems.
files.conclusion: The rendered TPDB texts are printed and their exact-match theorems resolve.

files.summary: This file defines the IO entry point main for the TPDB export verifier. It compares the ko7_full_step_tpdb exporter against its embedded checked literal and the on-disk Artifacts/ttt2/KO7_full_step.trs file. It then repeats the same embedded-versus-disk check for the free_recursor_tpdb export at Artifacts/ttt2/free_recursor.trs, returning nonzero on any mismatch.
files.conclusion: If main returns 0, both TPDB exporters match their embedded literals and on-disk artifacts.

files.summary: This file is the Lake build configuration for the OperatorKO7 package. It declares the OperatorKO7 library with its root module and sets additional Lean arguments. It declares the verifyTpdbExport executable rooted at VerifyTpdbExport and pins the mathlib dependency to a specific git revision.
files.conclusion: This file proves no mathematical result; it configures the package, its verifier executable, and its mathlib revision.
